subject: FinBridge pilot: packaging, batching/caching & quantization guidance

Subject: Proposal: FinBridge pilot packaging + quant/batch guidance

Marcus —

Can you and Kim put together two commercial packaging options (pilot-first and throughput-commit) and a short operational checklist for the pilot run? Dylan — please include a simple ops acceptance/test checklist we can give their SREs.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@finbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: FinBridge pilot packaging + quant/batch guidance

Elaine / FinBridge team — looping you in with our initial framing.

Quick summary of recommended technical approach (short bullets):
- Cache-first pilot: enable prefix/KV caching for stable prompt prefixes (expected ~35% hit rate given the profile). This reduces per-token CPU/GPU work for short, repetitive queries.
- Batching: configure adaptive batching with a 40ms latency cap for online paths and a larger batch window (200ms) for non-critical throughput. We expect a ~12-18% token-cost reduction when combined with cache.
- Quantization: run an A/B on int8 (quantized) vs fp16 (baseline) for model variants. Start with our quant-aware kernels and fall back to fp16 when quality delta exceeds 2% on the evaluation set. Expect latency improvements of 20–35% on int8 for long-context workloads, with modest quality tradeoffs on hallucination-sensitive prompts.

Commercial packaging (two options):
1) Pilot-first (no long-term commit): 90-day pilot; discounted rate = 15% off standard hosted token price; includes up to $6k in engineering credits for runtime tuning (applied to first invoice).
2) Throughput-commit: 6-month reserved capacity band with a 12% base discount + up to 10% performance rebate tied to meeting latency p95 <= 300ms and cache-hit >= 30%. Rebate paid as service credit quarterly.

We should also include a measured rollback clause for quantization: a documented threshold for reverting to fp16 if eval regressions breach agreed thresholds (we'll draft language).

Dylan — can you draft the ops acceptance checklist and add expected telemetry hooks (per-route token/tail-latency, cache-hit metric, quant-fallback events)? Kim — can you create two sketch SOW pricing lines we can hand to procurement? I'll package this into a short MAP for FinBridge to sign.

Attachments: quant_a_b_plan.pdf (planning doc)

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

From: Elaine Park <elaine@finbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: FinBridge pilot packaging + quant/batch guidance

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from Ops and procurement: 

1) Traffic profile: attached spreadsheet (FinBridge_traffic_profile.xlsx) — average QPS ~120, peak ~950 sustained for short bursts. About 60% of calls are sub-128-token classification requests (high duplication), 40% are long-context summarization (2–3k tokens).
2) Quantization risk: our compliance team is nervous about any quality regressions for summarization. Can you quantify how you'll measure the 2% delta? Is that on ROUGE/EM or a bespoke rubric?
3) Latency SLO: we'd like p95 <= 300ms for short requests and p95 <= 1.2s for long-context. Are those realistic with the suggested cache+batches?
4) Contract rollback: procurement wants a clause allowing us to force immediate rollback of quantized variants without penalty if we find production regressions. Is that acceptable?

If you can incorporate these into the MAP and SOW, we can move to procurement review next week.

—Elaine Park
Head of Platform Ops, FinBridge
elaine@finbridge.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finbridge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: FinBridge pilot packaging + quant/batch guidance

Elaine — good questions, thanks. Answers inline: 

1) Measurement for the 2% delta: we recommend a dual-track evaluation: (a) automated metrics (ROUGE-L for summarization + token-level accuracy on labeled QA set) and (b) a small human-eval of 200 samples focused on hallucination and instruction-following. The 2% is on a combined normalized metric we'll agree on in the MAP. We can supply the evaluation harness so FinBridge can reproduce results.

2) Latency SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for short requests is realistic with a 30–35% cache hit and adaptive batching (we'll size batch windows conservatively in the pilot). Long-context p95 <= 1.2s is achievable on our dedicated variants with the int8 kernels; expect slightly higher variance at peak load. We'll include autoscaling guardrails.

3) Rollback: acceptable — we'll include explicit rollback language allowing FinBridge to request immediate reversion to fp16 variants. We will require a short nomination period to activate rollback (we suggest window = 2 hours) and a joint post-mortem. No commercial penalties for rollback during the pilot.

Commercial tweak (concession): if FinBridge signs the Throughput-commit option within 30 days of pilot close, we'll bump the base discount from 12% to 15% for the first 3 months. Also proposing an operational credit: 10% invoice credit if we miss the latency p95 target more than twice in a 90-day window (capped).

Attached is our quant A/B plan (quant_a_b_plan.pdf) with test harness details and expected telemetry.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: FinBridge pilot: packaging, batching/caching & quantization guidance — mutual action plan (MAP)

Elaine / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a concise MAP that captures the technical plan, commercial options, and clear next steps. Key points:
- Pilot start target: 2026-11-16 (90 days) — FinBridge to onboard SREs and provide API keys/whitelist by 2026-11-12.
- Technical: enable prefix KV cache + adaptive batching. Run int8 A/B against fp16 for long-context; fall back on quality rules defined in the MAP.
- Commercial: Pilot-first = 15% pilot discount + $6k tuning credit. Throughput-commit = 6 months, 12% base + performance rebate up to 10%; 30-day signature concession to 15% base.
- Governance: rollback clause included; joint post-mortem within 5 business days of any rollout reversal.

Next steps (action items):
1) FinBridge: confirm pilot start date and return the signed MAP/SOW (DocuSign link below).
2) Redwood: finalize telemetry dashboard and send runbook to SREs (Dylan).
3) Procurement: FinBridge to send any procurement-specific language by 2026-11-10 for redlines.
